Glassnode: Bitcoin Hashrate Falls 8% YoY, First Annual Decline Since China's 2021 Mining Ban Glassnode said Bitcoin’s hashrate has declined approximately 8% year-over-year, marking its first annual contraction since China’s 2021 Bitcoin mining ban. Unlike the policy-driven decline in 2021, the current contraction is driven by falling BTC prices and deteriorating mining profitability, prompting some miners to shut down their machines. Bitcoin’s hashprice has reached an all-time low, further increasing financial pressure on miners. — link

Coinkite Releases Coldcard Security Incident Postmortem as 1,778.84 BTC Stolen From Over 8,600 Addresses Bitcoin hardware wallet maker Coinkite has released its postmortem on Coldcard’s seed-generation flaw, confirming that attackers reconstructed private keys offline rather than compromising the devices. A firmware configuration error disabled the hardware random number generator, causing devices to rely on an insecure pseudorandom number generator. At least 15 independent review and security research efforts between 2021 and 2026 failed to identify the flaw, including a review using OpenAI’s Cybersecurity Harness. Coinkite received 300 loss-related support tickets involving 236 customer accounts, approximately 0.2% of its estimated user base. According to Galaxy Research, 1,778.84 BTC were stolen from over 8,600 addresses, worth approximately $107 million at current prices. Coinkite released patched firmware on July 31 but warned that firmware updates cannot secure previously affected seeds. The attackers remain unidentified, and Coinkite has yet to decide whether to compensate affected customers. — link
